requestKey: Best budgeting app for irregular income|pocketpal.me|sample2

payload.text:
Here are the budgeting apps that handle irregular/variable income best, and why:

- Best overall: YNAB (You Need A Budget)
  - Built around “budget only the money you have,” sinking funds for non‑monthly bills, and an “Age of Money” metric that helps you build a buffer so lean months don’t hurt. Their workflow explicitly addresses irregular income. ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/guide/irregular-income?utm_source=openai))

- Best if you like spreadsheets or freelance/gig workflows: Tiller
  - Bank feeds flow into Google Sheets/Excel, with cash‑flow and paycheck templates you can customize for per‑project or per‑invoice income. ([tiller.com](https://tiller.com/cash-flow-spreadsheet-templates/?utm_source=openai))

- Best for predicting balances between inconsistent paychecks: Quicken Simplifi
  - “Projected Cash Flow” forecasts account balances using upcoming income/bills, and Planned Spending supports rollovers so unused funds carry forward. Great for seeing if a slow month will dip your checking. ([support.simplifi.quicken.com](https://support.simplifi.quicken.com/en/articles/3357429-using-projected-cash-flow?utm_source=openai))

- Best for flexible rollovers + modern goals: Monarch Money
  - Category rollovers are first‑class, and the 2026 updates added deeper Forecasting and Goals—useful when income varies and you need longer‑range planning. ([help.monarchmoney.com](https://help.monarchmoney.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411119762196-Rollover-budget-feature?utm_source=openai))

- Low‑friction automation with rollovers: Copilot Money
  - Auto‑categorization and simple budgets; supports category rollovers across months, though it isn’t a pure zero‑based tool. ([help.copilot.money](https://help.copilot.money/en/articles/3790828-budget-rollovers?utm_source=openai))

- Manual envelopes (no bank linking): Goodbudget
  - Classic envelope method; you record each inflow and “fill” envelopes—handy if you prefer manual control with irregular pay. ([goodbudget.com](https://goodbudget.com/help/?utm_source=openai))

Quick pick guide
- Want strict zero‑based with a built‑in buffer strategy: YNAB. ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/guide/irregular-income?utm_source=openai))
- Need cash‑flow projections to time bills vs. paydays: Simplifi or Monarch. ([support.simplifi.quicken.com](https://support.simplifi.quicken.com/en/articles/3357429-using-projected-cash-flow?utm_source=openai))
- Prefer full control/custom modeling (contractors/freelancers): Tiller. ([tiller.com](https://tiller.com/cash-flow-spreadsheet-templates/?utm_source=openai))
- Want an easy, automated tracker with basic rollovers: Copilot. ([help.copilot.money](https://help.copilot.money/en/articles/3790828-budget-rollovers?utm_source=openai))
- Prefer to stay manual/offline: Goodbudget. ([goodbudget.com](https://goodbudget.com/help/?utm_source=openai))

How to set up for irregular income (works in any app)
1) Budget only cash on hand; avoid planning with future paychecks. In YNAB terms, that’s the core rule and what drives “Age of Money.” ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/guide/irregular-income?utm_source=openai))
2) Create an “Income Buffer” or “Deferred Income” category. Park new income there, then release a fixed “paycheck” to cover essentials each month.
3) Build sinking funds (true expenses) for annual/irregular bills so you can smooth them with monthly contributions. Turn on category rollovers where available. ([ynab.com](https://www.ynab.com/blog/what-is-a-sinking-fund?utm_source=openai))
4) Forecast near‑term cash flow if timing is tight (Simplifi/Monarch), or use a per‑pay‑period sheet (Tiller). ([support.simplifi.quicken.com](https://support.simplifi.quicken.com/en/articles/3357429-using-projected-cash-flow?utm_source=openai))
5) Refill priorities on each payday: necessities first, then sinking funds, then discretionary. As your buffer grows, aim to live on last month’s income. ([support.ynab.com](https://support.ynab.com/en_us/age-of-money-H1ZS84W1s?utm_source=openai))

If you share your platform (iOS/Android/Web), whether you want bank syncing or manual entry, and if you prefer zero‑based envelopes vs. “spendable left” forecasting, I can narrow this to one or two specific picks and a setup checklist tailored to you.
